spec_match.rationale: Reads PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes on the main thread and inside a real dedicated worker and diffs them — the exact surface the feature changes.

interactive.rationale: Enumerate button ran both threads and rendered the diff table (15 main vs 3 worker types on this build).

blurb_alignment.rationale: Matches the gap-not-absence framing: the worker lacks long-animation-frame while the main thread of the same browser has it.

edge_cases.rationale: Preserves each thread's own reported order deliberately; explains the browser-without-the-API case.

conformance.rationale: Suite correct; workers-support-long-animation-frame honestly FAILS on this build (5/6) because the feature is absent here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Live enumeration: worker supports mark/measure/resource only; the page stated the gap precisely; console clean.

accessibility.rationale: Table scoped, lists textual, visible focus.

openQuestions.title: Re-run the worker LoAF demos on a build where the suite passes 6/6
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 the worker's supportedEntryTypes has no long-animation-frame (5/6 conformance; the demos correctly show the gap). This matches the existing feature-level major question. When a build passes workers-support-long-animation-frame, re-exercise all three concepts so a real worker entry is captured and refresh the critiques.

summary: Verified on headless Chromium 153 (Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12) driven over CDP via a Playwright script — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud environment; desktop 1280×800 and mobile 360×740 DPR3 screenshots captured and inspected. The main-vs-worker diff is the cleanest possible statement of this build's real state.
